input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification provision: the numbering jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and there is no defence or hold-harmless language anywhere in the document. Other clauses nonetheless assume indemnities exist — Section 9.3 conditions our termination right on "the remedies required by Section 20.5" (a section that does not exist), Section 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 treats "indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims, and Section 30.5 refers to "an indemnified party" and "vested indemnity rights". As customer we therefore have no Vendor IP infringement or misconduct indemnity at all, which is the playbook walk-away outcome. We inserted a new Section 20 with the preferred Vendor defence and indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions, and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies at 20.5 (which also repairs the broken cross-reference), plus a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 20 (Indemnification) with a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, a narrow Customer indemnity, standard procedure, IP exclusions, and infringement remedies (resolving the dangling cross-reference in Section 9.3 to Section 20.5).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnification section at all, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one exists (9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 20.5). We have inserted a new Section 20 giving us a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of law, Vendor-caused data breaches and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard procedure, customary IP exclusions and infringement remedies, and a narrow reciprocal indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

ops.text: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

20.2 Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that content or materials provided by Customer to Vendor for use in the Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, provided that delayed notice reduces the indemnifying Party's obligations only to the extent it is prejudiced. The indemnifying Party controls the defence and settlement with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. No settlement that admits liability or imposes any obligation on the indemnified Party is effective without its prior written consent.

20.4 Vendor's obligation under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of the Services or Deliverables without Vendor's authorization, combination of the Services or Deliverables with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent that combination, or Vendor's compliance with written specifications supplied by Customer.

20.5 If an infringement claim is made or reasonably anticipated, Vendor shall, at its expense and at Customer's election where practicable, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected Services or Deliverables, or modify or replace them with a functionally equivalent, non-infringing alternative. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverables and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion and Fees paid for Deliverables Customer can no longer use. These remedies are in addition to Vendor's obligations under Section 20.1.
